rounds.text: The company is demonstrating exceptional top-line acceleration, with compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months reaching 133% [E16] and screen reasons highlighting a year-over-year sales increase of 116% [E55]. This commercial momentum is successfully flowing down to the bottom line, evidenced by a compounded profit growth of 103% over the trailing twelve months [E20] and a staggering net profit surge of 222% year-over-year [E57]. Operating margins are expanding dramatically, hitting 3% in March 2026—a 91 percentage point improvement over three years [E25]—and reaching 35% in the March 2026 quarter, which is a 103 percentage point jump from the same quarter a year ago [E26]. Furthermore, the technical setup is supportive, with the stock price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43], and the business is benefiting from operating within a Forest Materials sector tailwind [E61]. Conceded: [E31].

The valuation is fundamentally disconnected from intrinsic worth, with the DCF model placing intrinsic value at Rs 23 per share against a market price of Rs 38, resulting in an aggressive margin of safety of -67.1% [E38, E39]. This rich pricing requires a massive 23.0% earnings growth to be justified, significantly outpacing the 16.0% baseline assumption [E40]. Underlying financial fundamentals are deeply concerning, highlighted by a severe negative ROE of -96.45% and an atrocious return on assets of -19% [E8, E9]. Cash generation has completely broken down, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -1 Cr and a staggering free cash flow burn of Rs -7 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30, E31]. Furthermore, financial liabilities are mounting as borrowings climb to Rs 72 Cr alongside massive contingent liabilities totaling Rs.103 Cr [E33, E53]. Conceded: [E16].

Conceded: [E16], [E20], [E25], [E26], [E43], [E55], [E57]. While the bull highlights exceptional top-line and bottom-line acceleration alongside supportive moving averages, this growth fails to generate actual cash, as operating cash flow sits at a negative Rs 1 Cr and free cash flow plunges to negative Rs 7 Cr in March 2026 [E30, E31]. Furthermore, borrowings have expanded from Rs 63 Cr to Rs 72 Cr concurrently, while massive contingent liabilities of Rs 103 Cr loom over the balance sheet [E33, E53]. The DCF model exposes an intrinsic value of just Rs 23 against a market price of Rs 38, leaving a severe margin of safety of -67.1% [E38, E39]. Finally, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands a demanding 23.0% earnings growth—surpassing the 16.0% assumed in the base case—proving that these aggressive recent growth metrics are already fully priced in with no room for error [E40].
